title: Trách nhiệm nhà sản xuất · Discuss both views
prompt: Some people support making manufacturers pay for collecting and recycling their products, while others oppose it because of the risks it could create. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
instructions: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 250 words.

outline.purpose: Dạng discuss yêu cầu giải thích riêng vì sao mỗi phía tin lập trường của mình rồi đưa phán đoán của người viết. Trong bài này, cân nhắc trọng tâm là: Khi nhà sản xuất trả chi phí cuối vòng đời, thiết kế khó tháo rời không còn chỉ rẻ ở nhà máy. Pin thay được làm rõ liên hệ giữa cấu trúc sản phẩm và chi phí thu hồi. Phí đồng hạng có thể chỉ chuyển người trả tiền mà không đổi sản phẩm. Mức phí theo thiết kế và xác minh độc lập xử lý hành vi này; lời cam kết “tái chế” của chính hãng chưa đủ làm bằng chứng.
outline.content: Supporters argue that producer responsibility can encourage products that are easier to repair and recover. Opponents respond that companies may pass the entire charge to consumers while continuing to produce difficult waste. I find the case for producer responsibility stronger, but accept that opponents' concerns about higher prices require charges to change design incentives rather than merely transfer disposal bills.

paragraphs: Supporters argue that producer responsibility can encourage products that are easier to repair and recover. Opponents respond that companies may pass the entire charge to consumers while continuing to produce difficult waste. I find the case for producer responsibility stronger, but accept that opponents' concerns about higher prices require charges to change design incentives rather than merely transfer disposal bills.

Producer responsibility can encourage products that are easier to repair and recover. A firm that bears disposal costs has less incentive to use inseparable materials merely to reduce factory expenses. An electronics company might design a replaceable battery instead of sealing it inside a disposable device. This changes the design calculation before waste exists, rather than leaving local authorities to deal with a product whose construction makes recovery uneconomic. If every product attracts the same fee, firms may simply increase retail prices without making batteries or other components any easier to replace.

Companies may pass the entire charge to consumers while continuing to produce difficult waste. If the disposal charge is unrelated to how easily a product can be repaired or recycled, redesign brings little financial reward. A company may cover the fee through higher prices while preserving the materials and construction that created the waste problem. Fees should vary with product design and be backed by independent verification. Differentiated fees must reward verifiable improvements, because a charge unrelated to design gives firms little reason to choose repairability over a simple price increase. Evaluation should track design changes and verified material recovery, rather than treat the collection of disposal fees as proof that waste has fallen.

Supporters are right that disposal costs belong in manufacturing decisions, while opponents expose the weakness of uniform fees; verified, design-sensitive charges make responsibility more than an additional consumer expense.

paragraphs.quote: Companies may pass the entire charge to consumers while continuing to produce difficult waste. If the disposal charge is unrelated to how easily a product can be repaired or recycled, redesign brings little financial reward. A company may cover the fee through higher prices while preserving the materials and construction that created the waste problem. Fees should vary with product design and be backed by independent verification. Differentiated fees must reward verifiable improvements, because a charge unrelated to design gives firms little reason to choose repairability over a simple price increase. Evaluation should track design changes and verified material recovery, rather than treat the collection of disposal fees as proof that waste has fallen.
